### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6d0cd700160e01ad2133beb6b2835fe85fb90914` — the merge of head `90174d8bf4b1dde01590f53b95be344f8f3d6298` into base `18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 6d0cd700160e01ad2133beb6b2835fe85fb90914 && git checkout 6d0cd700160e01ad2133beb6b2835fe85fb90914

git fetch origin 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258 90174d8bf4b1dde01590f53b95be344f8f3d6298 && git checkout -B drift-repro 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258 && git merge --no-ff 90174d8bf4b1dde01590f53b95be344f8f3d6298
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `90174d8bf4b1dde01590f53b95be344f8f3d6298`
Local-runs: none
Independence: INDEPENDENT AGENT

Contract review of PR #23364 (#23225 slice 2, ADR-0138 card E2: the `/ui` and `/data` dispatcher-domain floors), rendered at 2026-10-14T02:13Z. Inputs: the card body and all eight comments (triage, both claims, both dev reports, slice 1's ACCEPT and landing note, this slice's ACCEPT), the PR body, its 14-file list, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on the head. The accepted record was read from `main`. The dev report and the dispatching seat's ACCEPT were weighed as claims against the diff, not as evidence. This note stays at function level.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, with my reading of it.

1. **`/ui` dispatcher domain: an anonymous caller is refused 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` as `handleUiRequest`'s first statement.** Right. D2 says everything off the six-class list answers 401, "once per domain, as the domain's first statement, never surface by surface". `/ui` is on no row of the closed list. On `main` the handler made no anonymous decision at all (read on `main`: the path parse is its first statement), so on a `dispatch()`-fronted host the guest envelope reached the protocol slot and was served, which is the D9 adoption-rule breach D2 closes. The floor sits ahead of the path parse and the protocol probe; both anonymous shapes (an unresolved context and the guest envelope) are pinned under cases A, B and C, with the signed-in control D unchanged (served, 501 without a protocol, 400 for a repeated type). The route through `dispatch()` is pinned anonymous 401 and signed-in 200 in the registry test with the protocol never asked.
2. **`/data` dispatcher domain: the same floor as `handleDataRequest`'s first statement.** Right, by the same sentence. The one thing that could have made it wrong is D2 class 4 (anonymous `object_operation` endpoints), and I checked it on `main`: declared endpoints are served from the transport's fallback seam (`setFallbackHandler` in dispatcher-plugin.ts, which calls `callData` with its own bound deps), never through `handleDataRequest`; the route ledger's `/apps` row records the same wiring. So no door class is narrowed by this floor, and the dev's H3 reading stands on the source, not only on the sweep. The floor precedes the 400 (no object) and the 428 (unresolved environment on a multi-tenant host), both of which the signed-in control still reaches.
3. **`/data` passes `method`, so a CORS preflight passes the floor; `/ui` passes no method.** Right. `shouldDenyAnonymous`'s own contract makes `OPTIONS` pass, and the preflight case is pinned for `/data`. `handleUiRequest`'s signature carries no method on `main`, which is the same shape the `/keys` and `/notifications` floors took in slice 1; the Hono adapter answers a preflight itself with 204 ahead of `dispatch()` (its own test pins it), and the standalone server serves these paths from `@objectstack/rest`. Not a regression of any pinned behaviour.
4. **The floor is asked about the user id alone (no `isSystem`).** Right as the record's direction, see ③ for the residual. D2's own enforcement sentence is "`shouldDenyAnonymous` reads `userId`, which the guest envelope does not carry", and D9's guest envelope carries no user. `assembleExecutionContextOrGuest` decides anonymity as the absence of `authz.userId`, so every wire principal with an identity (a session, an API key, an OAuth agent whose `userId` stays the human) arrives with a user id, and the only caller this arm narrows is an in-process call of `HttpDispatcher.handleData` / `handleUi` or the two handlers with a system context and no user id. On `main` the only non-test callers of either handler are the registry entries and the two `HttpDispatcher` delegates (grep across packages, apps and examples). The changeset's last sentence names the in-process case.
5. **Public surface.** No export is added, removed or re-typed; the signatures of `handleUiRequest`, `handleDataRequest`, `HttpDispatcher.handleUi` and `handleData` are unchanged; `@objectstack/core` is untouched; `packages/qa/dogfood` is private. The changeset's description of what moves matches the diff sentence by sentence. Right.
6. **The matrix.** Two `enforced` rows with `covers` (the gate pin plus the dispatcher-domain ledger key each), two `GATE_PIN` probes on the two domain files, `DOMAIN_FLOOR_GATE_KEYS` 8 to 10, the two dispatcher-domain keys removed from the shrink-only baseline with `LEDGER_POPULATION_BASELINE_MAX` 26 to 24, `PROBE_TABLE` 23/18/29 to 25/20/33, `MATRIX_HEADER_PROBE_CLAIM` 23 to 25, the header figures 65 to 67 rows, 58 to 60 enforced, 29 to 33 keys, 10 to 12 gate pins, and the census note 12 to 14 classified, 11 to 9 in the baseline, 8 to 6 unnamed domain files. I re-derived each delta from the row and key counts the diff adds and removes; the arithmetic is consistent throughout, and the baseline's dispatcher-domain list is exactly the 9 it claims. The stale "Each of the 20 probes" sentence is corrected to 25 together with the pin that reads it. Right.
7. **The four runtime tests outside the claim's named paths.** Each signed its incidental anonymous caller in and gained an anonymous 401 plus `UNAUTHENTICATED` pin beside it; `http-dispatcher.ts` is not in the file list, so #23245's hold is respected. The claim comment was widened in place to name them. Right. The scoped-URL test's "domain ran" signal moving from the body's 503 to the floor's 401 is the floor doing what D2 orders (the decision precedes the service probe). Right.
8. **Negative controls.** Every refusal pin asserts status 401 and code `UNAUTHENTICATED`, with nothing resolved; the gate pins make a deleted floor read STALE and a probe minting no key read DEAD PROBE. The two ablations the dev reports (each floor's condition replaced by false, red declared first, restore proven against HEAD) are claims consistent with the pins the diff carries. Right.

**Gate verdicts on the head**, latest run per name at this record's reading: 29 success, 8 skipped, 3 still in progress (`Test Core (2/6)`, `(3/6)` and `(4/6)`), no failure. `Check Changeset`, both `Lint` batteries, every `Type Check` job, the governed-surface guard, the single-writer-path guard and the Part-of guard are success. Honest reading, as on slice 1: no pull-request check runs `@objectstack/dogfood` (its shards skip on `pull_request`), so the matrix, baseline and census edits rest on the dev's local 128/128 and the record reading the test code; `main`'s next battery is their first CI verdict.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset:** `.changeset/23225-ui-data-domain-floor.md`, `@objectstack/runtime: minor`, `fix(runtime)!:`, with the launch-window BREAKING line. Right: published runtime code narrows what an unauthenticated caller is answered on two domains, no export moves, and this is the exact shape slice 1's changeset took for the same change class and passed its contract review with. `packages/qa/dogfood` is private and owes none; `@objectstack/core` is untouched. Not `skip-changeset`.
- **ADR-0087:** `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Right: no authorable key, stored shape or exported declaration moves; the remedy is to sign in. The card row's `registered` semantic entry belongs to D2b, which this PR does not touch and the card stays open for.
- **`Clause-②:` line:** PR body line 2 reads `Clause-②: no (narrowing: ...)`, the value `no` with the `narrowing` arm, and the changeset carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Right: a card that narrows a published accept set is `Clause-②: no` and owes one contract-tier review before the queue, which this record is. The title's `!` matches the arm. `Check Changeset` is success on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dev `open_questions` (the one entry): keep the user-id-only floor (A) or also pass `isSystem` (B).** Ruled: A is the record's direction and is accepted here, not a new decision. D2's enforcement sentence names `userId`; D9's guest envelope carries none; slice 1's `/notifications` and `/keys` floors took the same arm and passed review; A is the strictly narrower answer on a security card. The residual is real and named: the cloud tree was not read, and a cloud host that calls the `HttpDispatcher` delegate in-process with a system context and no user id would now be refused. Escalated to the seat as a census item, not as a blocker: the changeset already names the case, and the move to B is small if a caller is found. The pre-existing split inside the floor family (`/analytics`, `/i18n`, `/meta` pass `isSystem`; `/notifications`, `/keys`, `/ui`, `/data` do not) is not this slice's to settle and is noted for the seat.
2. **Dev flag: `/ui` takes no method.** Answered in ①.3: accepted, the `/keys` shape, with the adapter answering preflight ahead of `dispatch()`.
3. **Dev `deviations`:** the widened file surface (the claim was updated in place: closed); the matrix header's stale probe sentence (in scope, pinned: closed); the merge commit carrying no trailer pair (process only; a squash takes the PR title: no contract effect); the one-time reach probe not committed (the PR's own acceptance note; agreed, and unavoidable while `@objectstack/rest` serves these paths on the booted showcase, so the `dispatch()`-door reach is unit-pinned only); zero label writes and the re-run after a lock timeout (no contract effect).
4. **Dev `out_of_scope_findings`:** the Hono catch-all rendering a declared status as 500 is filed as #23365 by the seat; the `/ui` view face serving every verb as the read was dropped by the seat. For the record: after this PR that behaviour sits behind the floor for an anonymous caller and is unchanged for a signed-in one, so it is not a D2 matter; it stays the seat's to ride the next edit of `ui.ts`. The view-route type drift between the two transports is an acceptance note. None blocks.
5. **Card scope still owed:** D2b (the publish refusal in both directions, its prescription and the `registered` ADR-0087 semantic entry) is not in this PR; the card stays open for it, and this record does not cover it.
6. **Checks in progress:** `Test Core (2/6)`, `(3/6)` and `(4/6)` were still running at this reading; the queue's own green-head requirement covers them. The dev's local full runtime suite (374 files, 6228 passed) is a claim, consistent with the diff.
